Use case: stylized-concept. Create real production sprite PART ART for a small 2D game healer appendage, matching the attached reference creature (a cream sprout bean with soft olive-green leaves): the same softly painted dimensional game-sprite rendering, clean dark colored contour, upper-left illumination, and simple readable materials at a final unit size of only 96 pixels. A squat elongated pear-shaped translucent golden sap pouch with a folded dark green leaf casing around its sides, one short leafy attachment pad on its right side for mounting flush to the creature's back, and a short green bottom outlet nipple. The pouch is clearly a liquid-filled reservoir, with a visible golden liquid surface, not a closed flower bud or fruit. The separate hose is a slender flexible dark-green plant vein containing pale gold liquid, descending in a gentle S curve and ending in a tiny rounded pale-gold healing tip directed downward-left.
Transparent PNG asset sheet with EXACTLY TWO independent isolated cutouts, no characters: LEFT HALF is the complete closed BACK-MOUNTED HEALING FLUID POUCH; RIGHT HALF is its complete downward healing hose. The two are coordinated parts of ONE natural IV-like apparatus: the hose top inlet will be attached directly to the pouch's bottom outlet in the rig. Provide intact contour and overlap at this joint, and generous transparent padding around each part. Pouch vertical aspect approximately 0.75 width to 1 height, compact flattened back side, not a hospital IV stand. Hose height approximately 0.8 times pouch height, diameter 1/8 pouch width, with a little connection socket at its top center and gentle one-bend downward slack. Do not include the creature, scene, hands, wheels, stand, straps crossing a face, lettering, labels, arrows, a grid, checkerboard pixels, drop shadow or glow clouds. A small contained luminous liquid highlight is enough. Fixed three-quarter front view compatible with a creature facing right; the apparatus sits behind the creature's left/back shoulder, with the right attachment pad going into the body. Keep both cutouts separated in two distinct vertical columns, upright and fully inside their own half of the transparent canvas.
